items.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021
items.q: The interviewer mentions Clark Terry in the context of liner notes and record appearances; the interviewee does not mention Clark Terry or indicate any personal interaction.

ctx.x: No. I’m a little too disorganized for that. I mean to have this sort of, I’m pretty much a more spontaneous type of person, however, I did know that I wanted to play, I got the most gratification from playing with great players, players that I admired, players that I looked up to. I aspired to play with the players that I used to listen to on records that were in New York. I got great satisfaction out of being able to be on the bandstand and to be making music with my idols. And that was the type of career path…

I see a collection of LPs behind you. And I know I used to spend many hours reading liner notes and almost like keeping track of how many LPs does Clark Terry show up on? And that kind of thing. And I wondered if you did that and did you envision some day seeing your name? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

No. I didn’t really think like that. I’m not — I have a lot of records here but I’m not really a real record collector. I’m not a completist, you know. I have a lot of Jackie McLean records but I don’t have them all. I have a lot of records of particular artists but there are some that I don’t have that maybe a lot of people have in their collections, I just didn’t get around to it. I never really — I never really thought of like, okay one day I’m going to have a hit record, I’m going to do everything I can to be…
